stem: The graph of \( y = f(x) - k \) is shown in the xy-plane. If \(k\), \(a\), and \(b\) are positive constants, which equation could define \(f\)?
whyCorrect: Start from the end behaviour. The curve rises on the left and on the right, so the degree is even — that alone kills both cubic choices. Then use the two minimum points: they sit at the same height, and \( y = f(x)-k \) is just \(f\) pushed down \(k\) units, so \(f\) itself has two equal minimum values, each equal to 0. A quartic whose two minima are both 0 is a perfect square with two double roots, one at a negative \(x\) (about \(-1.5\)) and one at a positive \(x\) (about 5), which is what \( f(x)=(x+a)^2(x-b)^2 \) gives with \(a\) and \(b\) positive.

whyWrong.A: This is a cubic with a positive leading coefficient, so it falls without bound on the left; the graph shown rises on the left. A cubic also has only one local minimum, not two.
whyWrong.B: Same problem as A — degree 3, so the left end goes down instead of up, and there is only one local minimum.
whyWrong.C: This has the same shape as the correct choice (a double root at a positive \(x\) and a double root at a negative \(x\)), so it is not distinguishable from D; see the note.

note: DEFECT: choices C and D are equivalent. With a and b any positive constants, (x-a)^2(x+b)^2 and (x+a)^2(x-b)^2 both describe a quartic with one positive and one negative double root, so both fit the graph. The item has two correct answers.

stem: \[ f(x) = m\sqrt{-x-n} \]where \(m\) and \(n\) are constants. If \( f(8)=0 \) and \( f(4) < -16 \), which of the following must be true?
whyCorrect: Pin down \(n\) first. \( f(8) = m\sqrt{-8-n} = 0 \) forces either \(m=0\) or the radical to be 0, and \(m=0\) would make \(f(4)=0\), which contradicts \( f(4) < -16 \). So \( -8-n = 0 \), giving \( n = -8 \) and \( f(x) = m\sqrt{8-x} \). Then \( f(4) = m\sqrt{4} = 2m < -16 \), so \( m < -8 \). With \(n=-8\), \( n-m = -8-m \), and \( m < -8 \) makes \( -8-m > 0 \).

whyWrong.A: This reverses the inequality. Dividing \( 2m < -16 \) by 2 gives \( m < -8 \), not \( m > -8 \).
whyWrong.B: \( n+m=0 \) with \(n=-8\) would mean \(m=8\), a positive \(m\); then \(f(4)=16\), not less than \(-16\).
whyWrong.C: \( n+m > 0 \) means \( m > 8 \), the opposite sign for \(m\). It comes from treating \(m\) as positive after dropping the minus sign in \( f(4) < -16 \).

stem: \[ 8rx^2 - 80sx + 8r = 0 \]For the given equation, \(r\) and \(s\) are constants such that \( r > 0 \), \( s < 0 \) and \( \frac{r}{s} > k \). What is the least value of \(k\) that ensures that the equation has two distinct real solutions?
whyCorrect: Two distinct real solutions means the discriminant is positive: \( (-80s)^2 - 4(8r)(8r) > 0 \), i.e. \( 6400s^2 - 256r^2 > 0 \), so \( r^2 < 25s^2 \). Divide by \( s^2 \) to get \( \left(\frac{r}{s}\right)^2 < 25 \), so \( -5 < \frac{r}{s} < 5 \). Because \( r > 0 \) and \( s < 0 \), the ratio \( \frac{r}{s} \) is already negative, so the only part of that range that can bind is \( \frac{r}{s} > -5 \). The smallest \(k\) for which \( \frac{r}{s} > k \) still guarantees a positive discriminant is therefore \( k = -5 \).

stem:
The functions \(f\) and \(g\) are defined by the given equations, where \( x \ge 0 \). Which of the following equations displays, as a constant or coefficient, the maximum value of the function it defines, where \( x \ge 0 \)?
I. \( f(x) = 16(1.24)^x + 43 \)
II. \( g(x) = 8(0.72)^x \)
whyCorrect: Check whether each function even has a maximum on \( x \ge 0 \). In I the base is 1.24, greater than 1, so \(f\) grows without bound as \(x\) increases — there is no maximum value at all, so no number in the equation can display one. In II the base is 0.72, less than 1, so \(g\) decreases; its largest value on \( x \ge 0 \) is at \( x=0 \), where \( g(0) = 8(0.72)^0 = 8 \). That 8 is the coefficient sitting in the equation, so only II displays its maximum.

whyWrong.A: For I, the 43 is the minimum the graph approaches from above as \(x\) decreases, and on \( x \ge 0 \) the smallest value is \( 16+43 = 59 \). Either way it is a floor, not a maximum — an increasing exponential has no maximum.
whyWrong.C: This requires I to have a maximum, which it does not; a base greater than 1 makes the function unbounded above.
whyWrong.D: This misses that a decaying exponential does have a maximum on \( x \ge 0 \), reached at \( x = 0 \), and that its value there is exactly the coefficient 8.

stem: The expression \( 6x^4 + 17x^2 + 7 \) can be rewritten as \( (3x^2+a)(2x^2+b) \), where \(a\) and \(b\) are positive integers, or as \( (3x^2+c)(2x^2+d) \), where \(c\) and \(d\) are positive nonintegers. What is the value of \( a+c \)?
whyCorrect: Expanding \( (3x^2+a)(2x^2+b) \) gives \( 6x^4 + (3b+2a)x^2 + ab \), so you need \( ab = 7 \) and \( 3b+2a = 17 \). The integer pair is \( a=7 \), \( b=1 \) (the other order gives 23, not 17). The same two conditions with nonintegers: substitute \( d = \frac{7}{c} \) into \( 3d+2c = 17 \) to get \( 2c^2 - 17c + 21 = 0 \), whose roots are \( c = 7 \) and \( c = 1.5 \); the noninteger one is \( c = 1.5 \) (with \( d = \frac{14}{3} \)). So \( a + c = 7 + 1.5 = 8.5 \).

stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \( f(x) = \frac{x^2+ax+b}{2x+c} \), where \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) are constants. The graph of the function \(f\) in the xy-plane, where \( y = f(x) \), does not intersect the line \( x = 4 \). If \( f(5) = f(6) = 0 \), what is the value of \( a+b+c \)?
whyCorrect: A rational function is zero exactly where its numerator is zero, so \( f(5)=f(6)=0 \) means the numerator factors as \( (x-5)(x-6) = x^2 - 11x + 30 \), giving \( a = -11 \) and \( b = 30 \). The graph fails to meet the vertical line \( x = 4 \) only if \(f\) is undefined there, so the denominator vanishes at \( x = 4 \): \( 2(4)+c = 0 \), so \( c = -8 \). (The numerator is 2 at \( x=4 \), not 0, so this really is an asymptote.) Then \( a+b+c = -11+30-8 = 11 \).

stem: The function \(h\) is defined by \[ h(x) = -\sqrt{x^2+bx+c} \]The graph of \( y = h(x) \) passes through \( (2,0) \) and \( \left(0, -\sqrt{358}\right) \). If \( h(m) = 0 \), what is the greatest possible value of \(m\)?
whyCorrect: Use the second point first, because \( x = 0 \) kills two terms: \( h(0) = -\sqrt{c} = -\sqrt{358} \), so \( c = 358 \). The point \( (2,0) \) gives \( -\sqrt{4+2b+358} = 0 \), so \( 2b + 362 = 0 \) and \( b = -181 \). Now \( h(m)=0 \) means \( m^2 - 181m + 358 = 0 \); the discriminant is \( 32761 - 1432 = 31329 = 177^2 \), so \( m = \frac{181 \pm 177}{2} \), i.e. \( m = 2 \) or \( m = 179 \). The greatest is 179.

stem: \[ \sqrt[7]{p^4} = t^{\frac{5}{7}} \]In the given equation, \( p > 1 \) and \( t > 1 \). If \( t = p^{2n-1} \), where \(n\) is a constant, what is the value of \(n\)?
whyCorrect: Rewrite the radical as a power: \( \sqrt[7]{p^4} = p^{\frac{4}{7}} \), so \( p^{\frac{4}{7}} = t^{\frac{5}{7}} \). Raise both sides to the 7th power to clear the sevenths: \( p^4 = t^5 \), so \( t = p^{\frac{4}{5}} \). Since \( p > 1 \), the base is not 0, 1 or \(-1\), so equal powers of \(p\) force equal exponents: \( 2n-1 = \frac{4}{5} \). That gives \( 2n = \frac{9}{5} \) and \( n = \frac{9}{10} = 0.9 \).
note: Book prints the last sentence as two fragments ("If t = p^{2n-1}, where n is a constant. What is the value of n?"); joined into one sentence.

stem: In the xy-plane, a parabola has vertex \( (9,-14) \) and intersects the x-axis at two points. If the equation of the parabola is written in the form \( y = ax^2+bx+c \) where \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) are constants, which of the following could be the value of \( a+b+c \)?
whyCorrect: Notice that \( a+b+c \) is just \( y \) when \( x = 1 \). Write the parabola in vertex form, \( y = a(x-9)^2 - 14 \); since the vertex is below the x-axis and the curve still crosses it twice, the parabola opens upward, so \( a > 0 \). At \( x = 1 \), \( y = 64a - 14 \), and with \( a > 0 \) that is strictly greater than \(-14\). Only \(-12\) clears that bound (it needs \( a = \frac{1}{32} \)).

whyWrong.A: \(-23\) is below \(-14\), which would require \( 64a-14 = -23 \), i.e. a negative \(a\) — then the parabola opens downward from a vertex already below the x-axis and never crosses it.
whyWrong.B: Same problem: \(-19 < -14\) forces \( a < 0 \), contradicting a parabola with two x-intercepts and vertex \( (9,-14) \).
whyWrong.C: \(-14\) is the vertex's y-value, reached only at \( x=9 \); getting it at \( x=1 \) needs \( a=0 \), which is not a parabola at all.

stem: \[ y = ax^2+bx+c \]The function \(f\) is defined above, where \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) are constants. The graph of \( y = f(x) \) in the xy-plane passes through the points \( (-16,0) \) and \( (9,0) \). If \(a\) is an integer greater than 3, what is the smallest possible value of \( 3b-2a \)?
whyCorrect: The two given points are the x-intercepts, so factored form gives \( y = a(x+16)(x-9) = a(x^2+7x-144) \). Matching coefficients, \( b = 7a \), so \( 3b-2a = 21a-2a = 19a \) — it depends only on \(a\). Since \(a\) is an integer greater than 3, the smallest allowed value is \( a = 4 \), and \( 19(4) = 76 \).
note: Book labels the displayed equation with y but calls the function f in the prose; transcribed as printed.

stem: \[ f(x) = ax^2+bx+c \]The function \(f\) is defined above, where \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) are constants and \( 4 < b < 7 \). The graph of \( y = f(x) \) is such that \( f(1) = f(5) \). If \(b\) is an integer, what could be the value of \( ab \)?
whyCorrect: Equal outputs at \( x=1 \) and \( x=5 \) put the axis of symmetry halfway between them, at \( x = 3 \). So \( -\frac{b}{2a} = 3 \), which rearranges to \( b = -6a \), i.e. \( a = -\frac{b}{6} \). The integers strictly between 4 and 7 are 5 and 6, and \( ab = -\frac{b^2}{6} \); taking \( b = 6 \) gives \( a = -1 \) and \( ab = -6 \).
note: Nothing in the stem forces a to be an integer, so b = 5 (a = -5/6, ab = -25/6) also satisfies every stated condition. -6 is the intended value; a grader should accept -25/6 as well.

stem: \[ f(x) = \sqrt[3]{x^3+ax^2+bx+c} \]The function \(f\) is defined by the given equation, where \(a\), \(b\), \(c\) are integers. The graph of \( y = f(x) \) passes through the point \( (9,0) \), and \( f(0) = 27 \). What is the value of \( 9a+b \)?
whyCorrect: A cube root is 0 only when its radicand is 0, so \( f(9)=0 \) gives \( 729 + 81a + 9b + c = 0 \). The other condition is easier: \( f(0) = \sqrt[3]{c} = 27 \), so \( c = 27^3 = 19{,}683 \). Substituting, \( 81a + 9b = -729 - 19{,}683 = -20{,}412 \). The question asks for \( 9a+b \), which is that expression divided by 9: \( -20{,}412 \div 9 = -2{,}268 \).

stem: \[ y = ax^2+bx+c \]The equation of a parabola is given, where \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) are constants. In the xy-plane, the parabola has vertex \( (3,11) \) and \( c < 0 \). Which of the following could be the value of \(b\)?
whyCorrect: The vertex's x-coordinate gives \( -\frac{b}{2a} = 3 \), so \( b = -6a \). The constant \(c\) is the y-intercept, and from vertex form \( y = a(x-3)^2+11 \) that is \( c = 9a+11 \). Requiring \( c < 0 \) gives \( a < -\frac{11}{9} \), and multiplying by \(-6\) flips the inequality: \( b = -6a > \frac{66}{9} = 7\frac{1}{3} \). Only 8 exceeds that.

whyWrong.A: \( b=5 \) gives \( a = -\frac{5}{6} \) and \( c = 9\left(-\frac{5}{6}\right)+11 = 3.5 \), which is positive, so \( c < 0 \) fails.
whyWrong.B: \( b=6 \) gives \( a = -1 \) and \( c = 2 \) — still positive.
whyWrong.C: \( b=7 \) gives \( a = -\frac{7}{6} \) and \( c = 11 - 10.5 = 0.5 \), positive by a hair. This is the trap: \(b\) must exceed \( \frac{22}{3} \approx 7.33 \), not just 7.

stem: The solutions to \( x^2+12x+35 = 0 \) are \(r\) and \(s\), where \( r < s \). The solutions to \( x^2+12x+27 = 0 \) are \(t\) and \(u\), where \( t < u \). The solutions to \( x^2+24x+c = 0 \), where \(c\) is a constant, are \( r+u \) and \( s+t \). What is the value of \(c\)?
whyCorrect: Factor each of the first two. \( x^2+12x+35=(x+5)(x+7) \) gives roots \(-7\) and \(-5\), so \( r=-7 \) and \( s=-5 \). \( x^2+12x+27=(x+3)(x+9) \) gives \(-9\) and \(-3\), so \( t=-9 \) and \( u=-3 \). The new roots are \( r+u = -10 \) and \( s+t = -14 \); their sum is \(-24\), which matches the \( 24x \) term and confirms the pairing. The constant term is the product of the roots: \( c = (-10)(-14) = 140 \).

stem: If \( p(x) = x^2+kx+4 \) has no real zeros, what is the range of possible values for \(k\)?

choices.label: D
choices.content: No range, \(k\) can be any real number.

whyCorrect: No real zeros means the discriminant is negative: \( k^2 - 4(1)(4) < 0 \), so \( k^2 < 16 \). Taking the square root of both sides of \( k^2 < 16 \) gives \( |k| < 4 \), which is the two-sided range \( -4 < k < 4 \), not a one-sided one. Large \(|k|\) in either direction is what forces the parabola to cross the x-axis.

whyWrong.A: This keeps only the negative half and, worse, has the inequality backwards — \( k < -4 \) makes \( k^2 > 16 \), so there are two real zeros.
whyWrong.C: Same error on the positive side: \( k > 4 \) gives \( k^2 > 16 \), a positive discriminant and two real zeros.
whyWrong.D: The discriminant does depend on \(k\); at \( k = 5 \), for instance, \( p(x) = x^2+5x+4 = (x+1)(x+4) \) has real zeros, so not every \(k\) works.

\[ f(x) = -3x^2+bx+c \]In the given quadratic function \(b\) and \(c\) are constants. The graph of \( y = f(x) \) in the xy-plane is a parabola that has a vertex at the point \( (h,k) \), where \(h\) and \(k\) are constants. If \( f(-4) = f(8) \), and the quadratic function has x-intercepts at \( (r,0) \) and \( (s,0) \), which of the following must be true?
I. \( r+s = 4 \)
II. \( b < 0 \)
III. \( c < k \)
whyCorrect: Equal outputs at \( x=-4 \) and \( x=8 \) put the axis of symmetry at their midpoint, \( h = 2 \). The x-intercepts are symmetric about that axis, so \( \frac{r+s}{2} = 2 \) and \( r+s = 4 \) — statement I holds. From \( -\frac{b}{2(-3)} = 2 \) you get \( b = 12 \), which is positive, so II fails. For III, \( k = f(2) = -12 + 24 + c = c + 12 \), so \( c \) is always 12 less than \(k\) and \( c < k \) always holds.

whyWrong.A: II is false: solving \( -\frac{b}{-6} = 2 \) gives \( b = 12 \). The sign trap is forgetting that the leading coefficient is \(-3\), which flips the sign of \(b\) you need for a positive axis of symmetry.
whyWrong.B: II is false for the reason above, and this choice also drops the true statement I.
whyWrong.D: Everything except II is right; a parabola opening downward does not force \( b < 0 \) — the sign of \(b\) follows from where the vertex sits, and here the vertex is at \( x = 2 > 0 \).

stem:
The functions \(f\) and \(g\) are defined by the given equations, where \( 2 \le x \le 8 \). Which of the following equations displays, as a constant or coefficient, the minimum value of the function it defines, where \( 2 \le x \le 8 \)?
I. \( f(x) = 0.0625(0.5)(2)^{x+2} \)
II. \( g(x) = 1500(0.2)^{x-3} \)
whyCorrect: Find where each function bottoms out on the interval, then see whether that number is actually written in the equation. \(f\) has base 2, so it increases and its least value is at \( x = 2 \): \( 0.0625(0.5)(2)^4 = 0.0625(0.5)(16) = 0.5 \) — and 0.5 is sitting there as a coefficient. \(g\) has base 0.2, so it decreases and its least value is at \( x = 8 \): \( 1500(0.2)^5 = 0.48 \), a number that appears nowhere in the equation. So only I displays its minimum.

whyWrong.B: \(g\) does attain its minimum at \( x=8 \), but that value is \( 1500(0.2)^5 = 0.48 \); the visible constants are 1500 (the value at \( x=3 \)) and 0.2 (the decay factor), neither of which is the minimum on \( 2 \le x \le 8 \).
whyWrong.C: Requires II, which fails; 0.48 is not displayed.
whyWrong.D: Misses that \( 0.0625(0.5)(2)^{2+2} \) collapses to exactly 0.5, so the 0.5 in the equation is the minimum value on the interval.

stem: The given expression is \[ -16(5x-3)^2 + 4(5x-2)^2 \]The given expression can be rewritten as \( \frac{ax^2}{4} + \frac{bx}{4} + \frac{c}{4} \), where \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) are constants. What is the value of \( a+b+c \)?
whyCorrect: Expand both squares and combine: \( -16(25x^2-30x+9) = -400x^2+480x-144 \) and \( 4(25x^2-20x+4) = 100x^2-80x+16 \), which add to \( -300x^2+400x-128 \). Now match that against \( \frac{a}{4}x^2 + \frac{b}{4}x + \frac{c}{4} \): every coefficient in the target form is divided by 4, so you must multiply by 4, not divide. That gives \( a = -1200 \), \( b = 1600 \), \( c = -512 \), and \( a+b+c = -112 \).

stem: Given the expression \[ \sqrt[4]{40n} \times \left(\sqrt[5]{40n}\right)^3 \]find the value of \(y\) for which the expression is equivalent to \( (40n)^{30y} \), where \( n > 1 \).
whyCorrect: Treat \( 40n \) as a single base and convert both radicals to fractional exponents: \( \sqrt[4]{40n} = (40n)^{\frac{1}{4}} \) and \( \left(\sqrt[5]{40n}\right)^3 = (40n)^{\frac{3}{5}} \). Multiplying powers of the same base adds the exponents: \( \frac{1}{4}+\frac{3}{5} = \frac{5+12}{20} = \frac{17}{20} \). Setting \( 30y = \frac{17}{20} \) gives \( y = \frac{17}{600} \).

whyWrong.B: \( \frac{10}{600} \) comes from \( 30y = \frac{1}{2} \), i.e. adding the exponents as \( \frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{4} \) and ignoring the cube on the fifth root.
whyWrong.C: \( \frac{7}{600} \) comes from \( \frac{1}{4}+\frac{3}{5} \) computed as \( \frac{1+3}{4+5} \)-style guesswork, or from subtracting instead of adding somewhere; the correct sum over the common denominator 20 is \( \frac{17}{20} \).
whyWrong.D: \( \frac{14}{600} \) corresponds to \( 30y = \frac{7}{10} \), which is \( \frac{1}{10}+\frac{3}{5} \) — the fourth root treated as a tenth root.

stem: \[ f(x) = 5(0.92)^{3x} \]The function \(f\) is defined by the given equation. The equation can be rewritten as \( f(x) = 5\left(1-\frac{p}{100}\right)^{x} \), where \(p\) is a constant. Which of the following is closest to the value of \(p\)?
whyCorrect: The two forms have the same coefficient, so the bases must match once the exponents are made the same. Use \( (0.92)^{3x} = \left((0.92)^3\right)^x \), and \( (0.92)^3 = 0.778688 \). So \( 1-\frac{p}{100} = 0.778688 \), giving \( \frac{p}{100} = 0.221312 \) and \( p \approx 22.1 \) — closest to 22.

whyWrong.A: 8 is the per-unit decay percentage before the exponent 3 is folded in: \( 1-0.92 = 0.08 \). That is the rate for one increase in \( 3x \), not for one increase in \(x\).
whyWrong.B: 12 does not follow from anything in the equation; it is roughly \( 3 \times 8 \) halved, and multiplying the rate by 3 is not how repeated decay works anyway.
whyWrong.D: 24 is \( 3 \times 8 \), the result of tripling the 8% rate. Compounding three times shrinks the total decay to 22.1%, because each 8% is taken off a smaller amount.

stem: Which of the following expressions has \( 6x-5b \) as a factor, where \(b\) is a positive integer constant?
whyCorrect: If \( 6x-5b \) is one factor, the other must be \( px+q \) with \( 6p = 24 \), so \( p = 4 \), and with constant term \( -5bq = -15b \), so \( q = 3 \). Multiplying out, \( (6x-5b)(4x+3) = 24x^2 + (18-20b)x - 15b \), so the middle coefficient has to be \( 18-20b \) for some positive integer \(b\): \(-2\), \(-22\), \(-42\), and so on. Only \(-22\) appears, at \( b = 2 \): \( 24x^2-22x-30 = (6x-10)(4x+3) \).

whyWrong.B: \( 18-20b = 18 \) needs \( b = 0 \), but \(b\) is a positive integer (and with \( b=0 \) the factor \( 6x-5b \) is just \( 6x \)).
whyWrong.C: \( 18-20b = 36 \) gives \( b = -0.9 \), neither positive nor an integer. A positive middle coefficient is impossible here, since \( 18-20b < 0 \) for every \( b \ge 1 \).
whyWrong.D: \( 18-20b = -484 \) gives \( b = 25.1 \), not an integer.

stem: \[ \frac{1}{cx} = \frac{x}{128} + \frac{1}{c} \]In the given equation, \(c\) is a constant. If the equation has exactly one solution, what is the value of \(c\)?
whyCorrect: Clear the denominators by multiplying every term by \( 128cx \): the left side becomes 128, and the right becomes \( cx^2 + 128x \). So the equation is the quadratic \( cx^2 + 128x - 128 = 0 \). Exactly one solution means a zero discriminant: \( 128^2 - 4(c)(-128) = 16{,}384 + 512c = 0 \), so \( c = -32 \). (Check: \( -32x^2+128x-128=0 \) reduces to \( (x-2)^2 = 0 \), and \( x = 2 \) does not make any original denominator zero.)
note: c = 0 would also leave one solution (x = 1) after clearing, but c = 0 makes 1/(cx) and 1/c undefined, so it is not admissible.

stem: The expression \[ bx^2-13x+22 \]can be rewritten as \( (hx-k)(x+j) \) where \(b\) is a constant and \(h\), \(j\), and \(k\) are integer constants. Which of the following must be an integer?
whyCorrect: Multiply out the factored form: \( (hx-k)(x+j) = hx^2 + (hj-k)x - kj \). Matching the middle term gives \( hj-k = -13 \), so \( k-13 = hj \) and therefore \( \frac{k-13}{h} = j \), which the stem already says is an integer. Nothing forces \(h\) itself to be \( \pm 1 \): for example \( h=-9 \), \( j=-1 \), \( k=22 \) gives \( -9x^2-13x+22 \), a valid case that kills the other three choices.

whyWrong.B: \( b = h \), and \(h\) need not divide 13. In the case \( h=-9 \), \( \frac{13}{b} = -\frac{13}{9} \).
whyWrong.C: From \( -kj = 22 \) you know \(j\) divides 22, not that 22 divides \(j\). With \( j=-1 \), \( -\frac{j}{22} = \frac{1}{22} \).
whyWrong.D: This is an integer only when \( h = \pm 1 \), which is not required; with \( h = -9 \) it is \( -\frac{1}{9} \).

stem: \[ f(x) = (x-a)(x-b) \]The function \(f\) is defined by the given equation, where \(a\) and \(b\) are integer constants. If \( f(32) > 0 \), \( f(35) < 0 \), and \( f(38) > 0 \), which of the following could be the value of \( a+b \)?
whyCorrect: The sign pattern positive, negative, positive means the graph crosses the x-axis somewhere between 32 and 35 and again between 35 and 38, so the two zeros \(a\) and \(b\) are trapped in those windows. Being integers, one of them is 33 or 34 and the other is 36 or 37. The possible sums are 69, 70, 70 and 71, and only 69 is offered (it comes from \( a=33 \), \( b=36 \)).

whyWrong.A: 35 is where the function is negative, not a sum of two zeros; the smallest possible sum is \( 33+36 = 69 \).
whyWrong.B: 37 is a single possible zero, not \( a+b \).
whyWrong.C: 67 would need the zeros to average 33.5, putting both below 35 — then \( f(38) \) and \( f(35) \) would have the same sign.

stem: In the given equation, \(k\) is a constant. The equation \[ \sqrt{k-x} = 43-x \]has exactly one real solution. What is the minimum possible value of \( 4k \)?
whyCorrect: Square both sides: \( k-x = x^2-86x+1849 \), so \( x^2-85x+1849-k = 0 \), whose roots are \( x = \frac{85 \pm \sqrt{4k-171}}{2} \). Squaring can create extra roots, so keep only those with \( 43-x \ge 0 \). If \( 4k-171 < 0 \) there is no real solution at all; if \( 4k-171 = 0 \) there is a single double root \( x = 42.5 \), which satisfies \( x \le 43 \), so exactly one solution. Any larger \(k\) either gives two valid roots (when \( 171 < 4k \le 172 \)) or one valid root again (when \( 4k > 172 \)), so the smallest \(4k\) that works is 171.
note: 4k > 172 also yields exactly one solution (the larger root then exceeds 43 and is extraneous), but 171 is the minimum.

The functions \(f\) and \(g\) are defined by the given equations, where \( 2 \le x \le 5 \). Which of the following equations displays, as a constant or coefficient, the maximum value of the function it defines, where \( 2 \le x \le 5 \)?
I. \( f(x) = -(x-4)^2+7 \)
II. \( g(x) = -(x+4)^2+7 \)
whyCorrect: Both are downward parabolas in vertex form, so each has maximum value 7 — but only at its vertex, and the vertex has to lie inside the interval. \(f\) has vertex \( x = 4 \), which is between 2 and 5, so \( f \) really does reach 7 there and the 7 in the equation is the maximum. \(g\) has vertex \( x = -4 \), far outside the interval; on \( 2 \le x \le 5 \) it is decreasing, so its greatest value is \( g(2) = -36+7 = -29 \), which is nowhere in the equation.

whyWrong.B: \(g\)'s vertex is at \( x=-4 \), not in \( 2 \le x \le 5 \); the 7 is a value \(g\) never attains on that interval.
whyWrong.C: Requires II, which fails on the vertex-location check.
whyWrong.D: Misses that \(f\)'s vertex \( x=4 \) is inside the interval, so \(f\) does attain the displayed 7.

stem: In the given equations, \(a\) and \(b\) are constants, \( a > 1 \) and \( b > 1 \). What is the value of \(x\)? \[ \sqrt[7]{a^5} = \sqrt{b^5} \] \[ a^{3x-3} = b^3 \]
whyCorrect: Convert the radicals to exponents: the first equation is \( a^{\frac{5}{7}} = b^{\frac{5}{2}} \). Raise both sides to the power \( \frac{7}{5} \) to isolate \(a\): \( a = b^{\frac{7}{2}} \). Substituting into the second equation gives \( b^{\frac{7}{2}(3x-3)} = b^3 \), and since \( b > 1 \) the exponents must be equal: \( \frac{7}{2}(3x-3) = 3 \), so \( 3x-3 = \frac{6}{7} \) and \( x = \frac{9}{7} = \frac{27}{21} \).

whyWrong.B: \( \frac{21}{27} = \frac{7}{9} \) is the reciprocal of the answer — it comes from writing \( b = a^{\frac{7}{2}} \) instead of \( a = b^{\frac{7}{2}} \).
whyWrong.C: \( \frac{32}{21} \) comes from solving \( 3x-3 = \frac{6}{7} \) as \( 3x = \frac{6}{7}+3 \) but then adding rather than dividing at the last step.
whyWrong.D: \( \frac{38}{21} \) follows from using \( a = b^{\frac{2}{7}} \) or otherwise inverting one of the fractional exponents; the exponent equation to solve is \( \frac{7}{2}(3x-3)=3 \).

Quadratic function \(h\) is defined by \[ h(x) = ax^2-2x+c \]where \(a\) and \(c\) are constants. The graph of \( y = h(x) \) in the xy-plane is a parabola that opens downward and has a vertex of \( (h,k) \), where \( k > 0 \). If \( h(1) = h(-13) \), which of the following must be true?

With \( b = -2 \), the axis is \( -\frac{-2}{2a} = \frac{1}{a} \), so \( \frac{1}{a} = -6 \) and \( a = -\frac{1}{6} \) — a single value, and it does lie strictly between \(-1\) and 0, so I must be true. For II, \( k = h(-6) = 36a + 12 + c = c + 6 \), and \( k > 0 \) only forces \( c > -6 \); taking \( c = -1 \) gives a legal parabola with \( k = 5 > 0 \) and \( c < 0 \).

whyWrong.C: I is true but II is not, for the reason above.
whyWrong.D: I is forced: the symmetry condition pins \(a\) to exactly \( -\frac{1}{6} \), which satisfies \( -1 < a < 0 \).

The vertex value is \( k = f(1) = -2+4+c = c+2 \), and \( k < 0 \) gives \( c < -2 \); anything less than \(-2\) is certainly less than \(-1\), so I holds too.

whyWrong.B: I is also forced: \( k = c+2 < 0 \) means \( c < -2 \), which implies \( c < -1 \).

stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \[ f(x) = 9x^2+kx-21 \]where \(k\) is a constant. In the xy-plane, the graph of \( y = f(x) \) passes through the points \( (r,23) \) and \( (2r,139) \), where \(r\) is a constant. Which of the following could be the value of \(k\)?

Putting \( r = 2 \) back gives \( 36+2k = 44 \), so \( k = 4 \) (and \( r=-2 \) gives \( k=-4 \), which is not offered).

whyWrong.C: 116 is what you get by keeping \( 9r^2+kr = 44 \) and \( 18r^2+kr = 80 \) but solving for \(kr\) instead of \(k\) and forgetting to divide by \(r\).
whyWrong.D: 162 comes from adding the two equations rather than subtracting, which does not eliminate anything usable.

stem: \[ 34z^{18} + bz^9 + 30 \]In the given expression, \(b\) is a positive integer. If \( qz^9+r \) is a factor of the expression, where \(q\) and \(r\) are positive integers, what is the greatest possible value of \(b\)?
whyCorrect: Substitute \( u = z^9 \); the expression is the quadratic \( 34u^2+bu+30 \), and you are factoring it as \( (qu+r)(su+t) \) with positive integers. Matching the ends, \( qs = 34 \) and \( rt = 30 \), and the middle coefficient is \( b = qt+rs \). To make \( qt+rs \) as large as possible, pair the two largest factors together and leave 1s behind: \( q=34 \), \( t=30 \), \( s=1 \), \( r=1 \), giving \( b = 34(30)+1(1) = 1021 \). Check: \( (34z^9+1)(z^9+30) = 34z^{18}+1021z^9+30 \).

stem: The function \[ v(x) = \frac{x^2+bx+c}{(x-7)(x-17)} \]where \(b\), \(c\) are constants goes through the points \( \left(0, \frac{99}{119}\right) \) and \( (11,0) \). There is another point where \( v(q) = 0 \). What is the value of \(q\)?
whyCorrect: Use \( x = 0 \) first, because it kills the \(b\) term: \( v(0) = \frac{c}{(-7)(-17)} = \frac{c}{119} = \frac{99}{119} \), so \( c = 99 \). A fraction is zero only when its numerator is, so \( v(11)=0 \) gives \( 121+11b+99 = 0 \) and \( b = -20 \). The numerator is then \( x^2-20x+99 = (x-9)(x-11) \), so the other zero is \( q = 9 \) — and 9 is not 7 or 17, so it is not cancelled by the denominator.

The function \[ f(x) = 6(x-a)(x-b)(x-c) \]is defined by the given equation, where \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) are distinct constants. When \( a < x < b \), the value of \( f(x) \) is positive. The graph of \( y = f(x) \) in the xy-plane contains the point \( (r,s) \), where \(r\) and \(s\) are constants. If \( s = 9 \), which of the following could be true?
I. \( r < a \)
II. \( b < r < c \)
III. \( r > c \)
whyCorrect: First order the zeros. A cubic with positive leading coefficient is negative below its smallest zero, then alternates: positive, negative, positive as \(x\) passes each zero. For \(f\) to be positive on the whole interval \( (a,b) \), that interval must be the first gap, so \( a < b < c \). Then \(f\) is positive exactly on \( (a,b) \) and on \( x > c \). Since \( s = 9 > 0 \), \(r\) has to sit in one of those two regions, and only \( r > c \) appears in the list.

whyWrong.A: For \( r < a \), \(r\) is below the smallest zero, where the cubic is negative — it cannot give \( s = 9 \).
whyWrong.C: III is possible but I is not, for the reason above.
whyWrong.D: On \( b < r < c \) the graph is between the second and third zeros, where a positive-leading cubic is negative, so II is impossible.

stem: \[ r(t) = 55t-2t^2 \]The function \(r\) is defined by the given equation. The function \(s\) is defined by \( s(t) = r(t)+1 \). Which expression represents the maximum value of \( s(t) \)?
whyCorrect: Adding 1 shifts the graph up, so the maximum of \(s\) is 1 more than the maximum of \(r\). The parabola \( r(t) = -2t^2+55t \) opens downward with vertex at \( t = -\frac{55}{2(-2)} = \frac{55}{4} \), and \( r\!\left(\frac{55}{4}\right) = 55\!\left(\frac{55}{4}\right) - 2\!\left(\frac{55}{4}\right)^2 = 2\!\left(\frac{55}{4}\right)^2 \), since \( 55 = 4 \cdot \frac{55}{4} \) makes the first term twice the second. So the maximum of \(s\) is \( 1+2\left(\frac{55}{4}\right)^2 \).

whyWrong.A: \( \frac{55}{2} \) is where \(r\) returns to zero, not the vertex; the vertex is at \( \frac{55}{4} \), half of that.
whyWrong.C: The subtraction has the parabola opening upward with a minimum. Here the leading coefficient is \(-2\), so the vertex value is a maximum and is positive.
whyWrong.D: Both errors at once: the wrong \(t\)-value and a sign that would make the maximum negative.

stem: The polynomial \[ 8x^4+50x^2+63 \]can be factored, and one of the factors is of the form \( (ax^2+b) \). What is one possible value of the product \( a \cdot b \)?
whyCorrect: Treat it as a quadratic in \( x^2 \): with \( u = x^2 \) you are factoring \( 8u^2+50u+63 \). Look for two numbers multiplying to \( 8 \times 63 = 504 \) and adding to 50 — those are 14 and 36. Splitting gives \( 8u^2+14u+36u+63 = 2u(4u+7)+9(4u+7) = (4u+7)(2u+9) \), so the polynomial is \( (4x^2+7)(2x^2+9) \). Taking the first factor, \( a \cdot b = 4 \times 7 = 28 \).
note: The other factor gives a valid answer too: 2 x 9 = 18. Both 28 and 18 should be accepted.

Expanding gives \( b^2+13b-68 = 0 \), which factors as \( (b+17)(b-4) = 0 \), so \( b = 4 \) or \( b = -17 \). Of these, only 4 is offered (check: \( a^c = 11 \), \( a^{2c} = 121 = 117+4 \)).

whyWrong.C: 110 is \( 117-7 \), the difference of the two y-values, which is not what the exponent relationship produces.
whyWrong.D: 124 is \( 117+7 \); adding the outputs ignores that doubling the input squares \( a^c \).

The functions \(f\) and \(g\) are defined by the given equations, where \( x \le 0 \). Which of the following equations displays, as a constant or coefficient, the maximum value of the function it defines, where \( x \le 0 \)?

stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \[ f(x) = ax^2+bx+c \]where \(a\), \(b\) and \(c\) are constants. The graph of \( y = f(x) \) in the xy-plane passes through the points \( (13,0) \) and \( (-6,0) \). Which of the following is the value of \( a+b \) in terms of \(a\)?
whyCorrect: The two points are the zeros, so the sum of the roots is \( 13+(-6) = 7 \). For \( ax^2+bx+c \) the sum of the roots is \( -\frac{b}{a} \), so \( -\frac{b}{a} = 7 \) and \( b = -7a \). Then \( a+b = a-7a = -6a \).

whyWrong.B: \( 6a \) is \( a + 7a \) with a sign slip, or \( a - (-7a) \); the sum is \( a + (-7a) \).
whyWrong.D: \( -7a \) is \(b\) itself, not \( a+b \).

stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \[ f(x) = 3x^2-5x+10 \]If the function \( f(x-2) \) is written in the form \( ax^2+bx+c \), what is the value of \( a+b+c \)?
whyCorrect: There is a shortcut: \( a+b+c \) is the value of the new quadratic at \( x = 1 \), and the new quadratic at \( x=1 \) is \( f(1-2) = f(-1) \). So \( a+b+c = 3(-1)^2-5(-1)+10 = 3+5+10 = 18 \). Expanding confirms it: \( f(x-2) = 3(x-2)^2-5(x-2)+10 = 3x^2-17x+32 \), and \( 3-17+32 = 18 \).

stem: In the given equation, \(p\) is a positive constant. The product of the solutions to the equation \[ (3x-7p)(5x^2+8x-4p)(x^3+3x^2-16x-48) = 0 \]is \( -\frac{560}{9} \). What is the value of \(p\)?
whyCorrect: Handle each factor separately. \( 3x-7p=0 \) gives the single root \( \frac{7p}{3} \). For \( 5x^2+8x-4p \), you do not need the roots themselves — their product is \( \frac{-4p}{5} \). The cubic factors by grouping: \( x^2(x+3)-16(x+3) = (x+3)(x-4)(x+4) \), whose roots multiply to \( (-3)(4)(-4) = 48 \). So the total product is \( \frac{7p}{3} \cdot \left(-\frac{4p}{5}\right) \cdot 48 = -\frac{448}{5}p^2 \). Setting that equal to \( -\frac{560}{9} \) gives \( p^2 = \frac{25}{36} \), so \( p = \frac{5}{6} \).

Which of the following below has a factor of \( 4x+7b \), where \(b\) is a non-positive integer?
I. \( 16x^2-49 \)
II. \( 16x^2+56x+49 \)
III. \( 64x^3+343 \)
whyCorrect: The constraint that \(b\) is non-positive is the whole question — the factor has to be \( 4x+7b \) with \( 7b \le 0 \), i.e. \( 4x-7 \), \( 4x-14 \), \( 4x \), and so on. I is a difference of squares, \( 16x^2-49 = (4x-7)(4x+7) \), and \( 4x-7 \) is \( 4x+7b \) with \( b = -1 \). II is the perfect square \( (4x+7)^2 \) and III is the sum of cubes \( (4x+7)(16x^2-28x+49) \); both have only \( 4x+7 \), which needs \( b = 1 \), a positive integer.

whyWrong.B: Both II and III factor with \( 4x+7 \) only, requiring \( b=1 \); III's quadratic factor \( 16x^2-28x+49 \) has a negative discriminant, so it contributes no other linear factor.
whyWrong.C: I qualifies but III does not, since \( 64x^3+343 = (4x+7)(16x^2-28x+49) \) forces \( b=1 \).
whyWrong.D: Only I contains a factor of the form \( 4x+7b \) with \(b\) non-positive.

stem: The equation \( N(m) = 63(Q)^{\frac{m}{6}} \) gives the predicted population \( N(m) \), in thousands, of a certain bacteria colony \(m\) minutes after the initial measurement, where \(Q\) is a constant greater than 1. The predicted population increases by \(p\)% every 180 seconds. What is the value of \(p\) in terms of \(Q\)?
whyCorrect: Convert the units first: \(m\) is in minutes, and 180 seconds is 3 minutes. Over 3 minutes the population is multiplied by \( Q^{\frac{3}{6}} = Q^{\frac{1}{2}} \). A growth factor of \( Q^{\frac{1}{2}} \) is an increase of \( Q^{\frac{1}{2}}-1 \) as a decimal, so as a percent \( p = 100\left(Q^{\frac{1}{2}}-1\right) \).

whyWrong.A: \( Q^{30} \) treats 180 as a count of minutes and divides by 6; the 180 is in seconds, so it is 3 minutes, not 180.
whyWrong.C: Two errors: the wrong exponent, and adding 1 instead of subtracting. The percent increase is factor minus 1.
whyWrong.D: The exponent is right but the sign is not: \( Q^{\frac{1}{2}}+1 \) would be the percent increase only if the population had started from zero.

stem: For the polynomial function \(v\), \( v(2) = 3 \) and \( v(0) = -13 \). The graph of \( y = v(x) \) in the xy-plane passes through the points \( (-2,7) \) and \( (6,0) \). Which of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.content: When \( v(x) \) is divided by \( (x+13) \), the remainder is 0.

choices.label: B
choices.content: When \( v(x) \) is divided by \( (x+7) \), the remainder is -2.

choices.label: C
choices.content: When \( v(x) \) is divided by \( (x+2) \), the remainder is 7.

choices.label: D
choices.content: When \( v(x) \) is divided by \( (x-6) \), the remainder is -13.

whyCorrect: The remainder theorem says dividing by \( x-r \) leaves the remainder \( v(r) \) — so you need the sign flipped when the divisor is written as \( x+r \). Dividing by \( x+2 \) means \( r = -2 \), and the point \( (-2,7) \) tells you \( v(-2) = 7 \), so the remainder is 7.

whyWrong.A: This asks for \( v(-13) \). The \(-13\) you were given is an output, \( v(0) = -13 \), not an input, so nothing is known about \( v(-13) \).
whyWrong.B: This asks for \( v(-7) \), which is never given; the 7 in the data is the output at \( x=-2 \).
whyWrong.D: Dividing by \( x-6 \) leaves \( v(6) \), and the point \( (6,0) \) makes that 0, not \(-13\).

stem: When the polynomial \( P(x) = 2x^3-5x^2+ax+b \) is divided by \( x-2 \), the remainder is 10. When \( P(x) \) is divided by \( x+1 \), the remainder is 1. What is the value of \( a+b \)?
whyCorrect: By the remainder theorem the two facts are \( P(2) = 10 \) and \( P(-1) = 1 \). Substituting gives \( 16-20+2a+b = 10 \), i.e. \( 2a+b = 14 \), and \( -2-5-a+b = 1 \), i.e. \( b-a = 8 \). Adding \( b = a+8 \) into the first equation gives \( 3a+8 = 14 \), so \( a = 2 \) and \( b = 10 \), and \( a+b = 12 \).

stem: \[ \frac{x^2}{\sqrt{x^2-c^2}} = \frac{c^2}{\sqrt{x^2-c^2}} + 39 \]In the given equation, \(c\) is a positive constant. Which of the following is one of the solutions to the given equation?
whyCorrect: Both fractions have the same denominator, so move them together: \( \frac{x^2-c^2}{\sqrt{x^2-c^2}} = 39 \). A quantity divided by its own square root is that square root, so this is just \( \sqrt{x^2-c^2} = 39 \). Squaring gives \( x^2 = c^2+39^2 \), so \( x = \pm\sqrt{c^2+39^2} \), and the negative one is listed.

whyWrong.A: \( x = -c \) makes \( x^2-c^2 = 0 \), so both denominators are zero and the expression is undefined.
whyWrong.B: This is \( x^2 \) with a sign error, not \(x\); you still have to take a square root, and \( -c^2-39^2 \) is negative, so its square cannot equal \( c^2+39^2 \).
whyWrong.C: Subtracting instead of adding: squaring gives \( x^2 = 39^2-c^2 \), which makes \( x^2-c^2 = 39^2-2c^2 \), not \( 39^2 \).

note: DEFECT in the book's typesetting: the +39 is printed under the right-hand radical, as c^2/sqrt(x^2-c^2+39). Taken literally that equation has no real solutions for any positive c (checked with sympy for c = 1, 5, 13, 20, 50 — all four roots complex), and none of the choices satisfies it. Transcribed with the 39 as a separate term, which is the only reading under which a listed choice works and which the choices themselves (all built on 39^2) confirm.

stem: The expression \[ 12x^2+41x+35 \]can be rewritten as \( (4x+r)(3x+s) \), where \(r\) and \(s\) are integers, or as \( (4x+t)(3x+v) \), where \(t\) and \(v\) are not integers. What is the value of \( s+v \)?
whyCorrect: Expanding \( (4x+r)(3x+s) \) gives \( 12x^2+(4s+3r)x+rs \), so you need \( rs = 35 \) and \( 4s+3r = 41 \). The integer pair is \( r=7 \), \( s=5 \) (the other order gives 43). For the non-integer pair, substitute \( v = \frac{35}{t} \) into \( 4v+3t = 41 \) to get \( 3t^2-41t+140 = 0 \), whose roots are \( t = 7 \) and \( t = \frac{20}{3} \); the non-integer one gives \( v = \frac{21}{4} \). So \( s+v = 5+\frac{21}{4} = \frac{41}{4} \).

whyWrong.A: \( \frac{41}{3} \) is \( t+? \)-style bookkeeping on the wrong pair — it is what you get by adding the two t-values \( 7+\frac{20}{3} \) and dividing, not \( s+v \).
whyWrong.C: 12 is the leading coefficient, not a sum of the two second constants.
whyWrong.D: 35 is the product \( rs \), the constant term.

stem: \[ x(9x-2a) + b(9x-2a) - (x+b) = 0 \]In the given equation, \(a\) and \(b\) are positive constants. A solution to the equation is \( x = 42 \). What is the value of \(a\)?
whyCorrect: Do not expand — factor. The first two terms share \( 9x-2a \), giving \( (x+b)(9x-2a) \), and the third term is \( -(x+b) \), so the whole left side is \( (x+b)(9x-2a-1) \). The solutions are therefore \( x = -b \) and \( x = \frac{2a+1}{9} \). Since \(b\) is positive, \( -b \) cannot be 42, so \( \frac{2a+1}{9} = 42 \), giving \( 2a+1 = 378 \) and \( a = 188.5 \).

stem: For a polynomial function \(f\), the graph of \( y = f(x) \) in the xy-plane contains the points \( (-6,0) \), \( (7,0) \), \( (0,0) \), and \( (4,0) \). Which of the following must be a factor of \( f(x) \)?
whyCorrect: Each listed point has y-coordinate 0, so \(-6\), 7, 0 and 4 are all zeros of \(f\), and a quadratic can only be a factor if both of its own zeros are on that list. Factor each choice: \( x^2-7x = x(x-7) \) has zeros 0 and 7, both on the list, so it divides \( f(x) \).

whyWrong.A: \( x^2-2x-24 = (x-6)(x+4) \), with zeros 6 and \(-4\) — the signs of the given zeros \(-6\) and 4 are flipped.
whyWrong.B: \( x^2-x+42 \) has discriminant \( 1-168 < 0 \), so it has no real zeros at all and cannot be built from these x-intercepts. It looks plausible only because \( -6 \times 7 = -42 \), and even that sign is wrong.
whyWrong.C: \( x^2-11x-28 \) does not factor over the integers; its zeros are \( \frac{11\pm\sqrt{233}}{2} \), neither of which is a listed zero.

stem: \[ f(x) = m\sqrt{-x-n} \]where \(m\) and \(n\) are constants. If \( f(8)=0 \) and \( f(4) < -16 \), which of the following must be true?
whyCorrect: \( f(8) = m\sqrt{-8-n} = 0 \) leaves two possibilities, and \( m = 0 \) is ruled out because it would make \( f(4) = 0 \), not less than \(-16\). So the radicand is zero at \( x=8 \): \( n = -8 \) and \( f(x) = m\sqrt{8-x} \). Then \( f(4) = 2m < -16 \) gives \( m < -8 \), and \( n-m = -8-m > 0 \).

whyWrong.A: The inequality points the other way: \( 2m < -16 \) gives \( m < -8 \).
whyWrong.B: With \( n = -8 \) this would mean \( m = 8 \), making \( f(4) = 16 \), which is not less than \(-16\).
whyWrong.C: \( n+m > 0 \) means \( m > 8 \) — a positive \(m\), when the condition forces \(m\) to be very negative.

note: Exact duplicate of question 19 in the same chapter of this book (identical stem and choices).

stem: \[ (3x+p)(5x^2-45)(2x^2-16x+6p) = 0 \]In the given equation, \(p\) is a positive constant. The sum of the solutions to the equation is \( \frac{20}{3} \). What is the value of \(p\)?
whyCorrect: Take the factors one at a time and use sums, not individual roots. \( 3x+p = 0 \) contributes \( -\frac{p}{3} \). \( 5x^2-45 = 0 \) gives \( x = \pm 3 \), contributing 0. For \( 2x^2-16x+6p \), the sum of the roots is \( \frac{16}{2} = 8 \), whatever \(p\) is. So the total is \( 8-\frac{p}{3} = \frac{20}{3} \), giving \( \frac{p}{3} = \frac{4}{3} \) and \( p = 4 \). (Check: at \( p=4 \) the last factor has discriminant \( 64-48 > 0 \), so its two roots 2 and 6 are real, and all five solutions are distinct.)

stem: In the xy-plane above, the function \(f\) is defined by \( f(x) = 2x^3+3x^2+ax+b \), where \(a\) and \(b\) are constants. If the graph of \(f\) intersects the x-axis at three points, what is the value of \(a\)?
whyCorrect: Read the two labelled zeros, \( x = -3 \) and \( x = 2 \), off the graph. For \( 2x^3+3x^2+ax+b \) the three zeros sum to \( -\frac{3}{2} \), so the third zero is \( -\frac{3}{2}-(-3)-2 = -\frac{1}{2} \). That makes \( f(x) = 2(x+3)(x-2)\left(x+\frac{1}{2}\right) = (x+3)(x-2)(2x+1) \); expanding gives \( 2x^3+3x^2-11x-6 \), so \( a = -11 \) (and \( b = -6 \), matching the labelled y-intercept).
note: Depends on the graph: the cubic is drawn with x-intercepts labelled -3 and 2, a third unlabelled crossing between them, and y-intercept -6.

stem: The graph of \( y = a(x+1)(x-5) \) is shown in the xy-plane above, where \(a\) is a constant. If the graph with vertex \( (h,k) \) intersects the y-axis at point \( (0,5) \), which of the following is equal to \(k\)?
whyCorrect: Find \(a\) from the given point: substituting \( (0,5) \) gives \( a(1)(-5) = 5 \), so \( a = -1 \). The vertex sits halfway between the zeros \(-1\) and 5, at \( h = 2 \). Then \( k = -(2+1)(2-5) = -(3)(-3) = 9 \).

whyWrong.A: 7 does not come from any consistent value of \(a\); with \( a = -1 \) the vertex height is fixed at 9.
whyWrong.B: 8 would be the vertex value if the zeros were \(-1\) and 5 with \( a \approx -0.89 \); the point \( (0,5) \) pins \( a = -1 \) exactly.
whyWrong.D: 10 is the result of using \( h = 2 \) but computing \( k \) as \( 5+5 \), adding the y-intercept to itself instead of evaluating the function at the vertex.

note: The graph is shown in the book (downward parabola through (-1,0), (5,0) and (0,5) with vertex labelled (h,k)), but every number needed is stated in the text.

stem: In the xy-plane above, the graph of a quadratic function \( y = f(x) \) intersects the x-axis at points \(O\) and \(Q\), and has a vertex at point \(P\). If line \( \ell \) passes through points \(P\) and \(Q\), what is the y-intercept of line \( \ell \)?
whyCorrect: \(O\) is the origin, so one zero is \( x=0 \), and the vertex \( P(3,5) \) sits halfway between the zeros — that puts \(Q\) at \( (6,0) \). The line through \( (3,5) \) and \( (6,0) \) has slope \( \frac{0-5}{6-3} = -\frac{5}{3} \). Going from \( P \) back to \( x=0 \) is 3 more units left, raising \(y\) by another 5, so the y-intercept is \( 5+5 = 10 \).
note: Depends on the graph: the parabola through the origin and (6,0) with vertex labelled P(3,5), and line l drawn through P and Q.

stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \( f(x) = x^3 \). The function \(g\) is defined by \( g(x) = a \cdot f(x+b)+c \), where \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) are constants. The graph of \( y = g(x) \) is shown in the xy-plane. Find the value of \( ab \).
whyCorrect: \( g(x) = a(x+b)^3+c \), so the point where the curve flattens out — its point of inflection — is \( (-b, c) \). The graph flattens at the marked point \( (4,6) \), giving \( b = -4 \) and \( c = 6 \). Then the other marked point \( (5,24) \) gives \( a(5-4)^3+6 = 24 \), so \( a = 18 \), and \( ab = 18(-4) = -72 \).
note: Depends on the graph: a cubic through the marked points (4,6) — its point of inflection — and (5,24).

stem: The graphs of \( y = x^2 \) and \( y = mx-1 \) are shown in the xy-plane below, where \(m\) is the slope of the line. If the graph of \( y = mx-1 \) is tangent to the graph of \( y = x^2 \), what is the value of \(m\)?
whyCorrect: Tangent means the two graphs meet at exactly one point, so set them equal and force a single solution: \( x^2 = mx-1 \) becomes \( x^2-mx+1 = 0 \), and one solution means the discriminant is zero: \( m^2-4 = 0 \), so \( m = \pm 2 \). The line in the figure slopes upward, so \( m = 2 \) (touching the parabola at \( x = 1 \)).
note: The algebra alone gives m = 2 or m = -2; the figure, which shows an upward-sloping line, is what selects +2.
